subtype: Approach: mental rehearsal of scam scripts [Thinking]
passage: Uncle Jagdish pinned a printed article to our fridge: fake officers, fake job offers, fake parcels. I read it twice and then did something a bit silly. In front of the bathroom mirror, out loud, I practised. “I will call the police station myself.” “I don't discuss money on the phone.” “Thank you, no.” I said them until they sounded boring, which was the point. A week later my phone rang. A grave voice said there was a parcel in my name with something illegal inside. My hands shook. But the lines were already in my mouth, and I said, “I'll call the station myself,” and ended the call. Then I told Mama and sat down. — Mehr

qa.q: Where did the narrator practise the lines?
qa.a: In front of the bathroom mirror.

qa.q: How did Mehr feel when the real call came?
qa.a: Nervous: Mehr's hands shook, but the practised words came out anyway.

qa.q: What else could Mehr add to the plan, and why?
qa.a: A rule to hang up and tell an adult whatever the caller says, since a calm exit works even when the story sounds frightening.

qa.q: How might Jagdish feel on hearing what happened?
qa.a: Jagdish, who pinned the article, may feel relieved and proud that the reading turned into a calm refusal.

grounding: After reading examples of frauds, a teen rehearses aloud what to say to a fake officer, so a calm refusal is ready.

Counsellor's note, cyber-safety club, Wednesday
Today's session used the booklet of common fraud examples. Most students read quietly. Mehak asked if she and Hafsa could act them out instead, and I agreed.
Hafsa played a “police officer” on a pretend call: “Your parcel had illegal items. Pay a fine or be arrested today.” Mehak's first answer was nervous: “But I didn't send anything...” She stopped and said to me, “If I argue, I'm already in the conversation. I need a line I can say without thinking.” She tried again: “I don't discuss this on calls. I'll go to the police station with my parents.” Then she put down the pretend phone.
They switched to a fake job offer asking for a registration fee. By the fourth try her refusal was steady and short.
Next week I will ask Mehak to lead a round with the Class Eight group.

qa.q: What line did Mehak settle on for the fake officer?
qa.a: I don't discuss this on calls. I'll go to the police station with my parents.

qa.q: Why did Mehak stop after her first nervous answer?
qa.a: Mehak felt uneasy arguing and saw she needed a ready line, so fear during a call wouldn't pull her into talking.

qa.q: What else could make Mehak's practice even more useful?
qa.a: Rehearsing with a parent at home too, so the family shares the same short lines and knows what to do if a real call comes.

qa.q: What is the practice like for Hafsa, playing the caller?
qa.a: Hafsa sees from the inside how pressure lines work, which likely makes those tricks easier to spot in real life.

grounding: A counsellor notes a teen rehearsing aloud what she would say to a fake officer and a fake job offer, so a calm refusal is ready.

passage:
Tuesday
It actually happened. Three weeks after Francis and I practised with that list of common frauds, a “job offer” call came during my evening walk. A woman said I'd been picked for a work-from-home data job and only needed to pay a small registration fee today.
Old me would have got excited, asked questions, maybe believed her. But Francis and I had said the lines out loud so many times on the terrace that my mouth just did it: “Real jobs don't ask for fees. I'm not interested. Please don't call again.” Then I cut the call.
My heart was still thumping afterwards, which is funny, because my voice was calm. I told Mummy when I got home, and we blocked the number.
Rehearsing felt silly back then. Francis kept doing a terrible accent. But it worked, and I didn't have to think at all.
– Deepika

qa.q: What did the caller say Deepika had been picked for?
What was Deepika feeling during and after the call?
qa.a: Deepika's voice was calm, but the heart kept thumping afterwards, showing nervousness underneath and then relief.

qa.q: What else could Deepika rehearse next with Francis?
qa.a: Replies to texts and links, not just calls, so a calm response is ready for every kind of trick.

qa.q: How might Francis feel hearing the rehearsal worked?
qa.a: Francis would likely be pleased and a little proud that the silly terrace practice, accent and all, paid off.

grounding: Shows a teen who rehearsed refusals aloud from a list of common frauds calmly turning down a real fake job call.
